comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Dutch regulations confirm the first two years and 30 EC of open study for the revised cohort. Appendix III separates the revised Years 1–2 from the old Year 3 table. VU’s current programme page names the final-year courses, but does not establish their credit allocation for September 2026 entrants. Article 9.1 specifies the general 90 EC thesis threshold excluding electives, including Academic Skills 1 and 2. Article 10.4 addresses the Dutch language test and remediation.

routeSelection.route: Dutch-language National Politics and Government route
routeSelection.basis: Registry resolution case rc-0074 (normalization status step2-resolved-split) explicitly identifies cp-000113 as the Dutch-taught 'Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' track/version of the shared VU Political Science registration, distinct from the English 'Global Politics' track (cp-000112); the registry's own targets metadata records {"language":"NLD","focus":"national politics and governance"} for this exact target. OER Article 10.2 confirms that, starting cohort 2025-2026, the bachelor's programme (RIO 56606) offers exactly two named tracks -- 'Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' (Dutch) and 'Political Science: Global Politics' (English) -- so the normalized target itself names this exact official route (Section 2.1 rule 1), confirmed by current official evidence for the 2026-2027 academic year and by the Dutch-language 'politicologie' curriculum, overview and future/career webpages themselves, and by Article 10.4's confirmation that Dutch is the track's language of instruction.

exception.curriculumContext: The verified curriculum covers Dutch and comparative politics, public management, law, economics, Europe and quantitative and qualitative political research.

audience.programmeDescription: This Dutch-language VU route studies political power and public administration in the Netherlands. Students examine democracy, the welfare state, Europe, economics and political thought. They develop research skills through quantitative and qualitative projects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: VU’s published materials confirm 150 of 180 EC for September 2026 entrants. The comparison shows the verified curriculum while the final-year credit allocation still needs confirmation.

curriculum.limitation: The verified 150 EC covers years one and two and a 30 EC open semester in year three. VU names the remaining courses, including the thesis project. Its published credit table applies to earlier entrants.
